name: Caffeine
short: Systematic review: up to 400 mg/day in healthy adults generally not linked to overt adverse effects (300 mg/day in pregnancy: reproductive/developmental effects); several grams can be toxic or lethal.
text: A systematic review of 381 studies concluded that the evidence generally supports that consumption of up to 400 mg of caffeine a day in healthy adults is not associated with overt adverse cardiovascular, behavioural, reproductive and developmental, acute or bone effects, and that up to 300 mg a day in healthy pregnant women is generally not associated with adverse reproductive and developmental effects; data for children and adolescents were limited, and the authors called for research in sensitive groups such as people with pre-existing conditions. A clinical toxicology review noted that quantities of several grams are known to cause toxicity and potentially death, and described as troubling cases of mainly younger individuals who had severe side effects or died after doses not otherwise known to cause such harm. A literature review in people after acute coronary syndrome found that interactions of coffee or caffeine with the common medicines used in that setting are little studied, and that the only interaction identified in human studies was with the protective effect of statins on cardiac ischaemia.
